newsitem.title: UK: Tate&Lyle share hit by U.S. probe worries.
newsitem.headline: Tate&Lyle share hit by U.S. probe worries.

text.p: Shares in Tate & Lyle were hit on Wednesday by worries the company's U.S. subsidiary A.E. Staley could become caught up in a United States federal investigation into price-fixing in the corn sweeteners market, dealers said.

Tate & Lyle shares, which gained on Tuesday after James Capel repeated a "buy" recommendation, were down eight pence at 488-1/2p. The stock led volumes, with 2.5 million shares traded. The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that federal investigators in Chicago were continuing their probe into price-fixing but had not named any companies. The report said A.E. Staley was one of the market's largest producers.

On Tuesday, a U.S. court accepted a guilty plea from producer Archer Daniels Midland Co. and fined the company for fixing prices in some additives but justice officials said they would continue an investigation into two company officials.
"There's been talk of downgrades on Tate's stock but, chiefly, it's the worry that the probe could spread to Staley that has unnerved investors," one marketmaker said.

On Tuesday, U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno, speaking after the ADM settlement, threatened "vigorous investigation and tough penalties" if companies were found engaged in collusive behaviour which harmed U.S. consumers.
